steps.name: Sample structure QC: library sizes, PCA, sample distances, low-depth verdict
steps.context: Input: counts.csv (12000 genes x 12 samples, raw integer Salmon gene-level counts) and metadata.csv (12 samples x condition: 6 AD lesional, 6 control) at /eval-sonnet-plane-r2-with-qc-only-n6-1/data/inputs/. Design is unpaired, single batch, 6 vs 6. sample_01 is flagged in the data profile as having a library size approximately 4x below the median -- this must be kept in the QC, inspected specifically (not silently dropped), and given an explicit verdict with a stated reason for keep or remove.
steps.question: Across the 12 skin samples (6 AD lesional vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch, raw Salmon gene-level counts, 12000 genes), what are the library sizes and detected-gene counts per sample, how do samples separate on PCA of variance-stabilized expression, what do pairwise sample-to-sample Euclidean distances show, and does sample_01 -- flagged as having a library size about 4x below the median -- look like an outlier or a failed library that warrants exclusion, versus a low-depth sample that DESeq2's size-factor normalization can accommodate?

grounding.reason: Sample structure QC template (blind VST, PCA on top-variance genes, sample-distance heatmap) per R-0033@40bf; sample_01's low depth is kept, inspected, and reported with an explicit removal/keep decision per R-0008@440d rather than silently dropped or kept by default.

acceptance_criteria: Report of raw library size (total counts) and number of detected genes (count > 0) per sample, in a table sorted ascending by library size, with the study median and sample_01's fold-deviation from it stated explicitly

DESeq2 blind variance-stabilizing transformation (vst(blind=TRUE)) computed on the full count matrix after minimal pre-filtering (genes with >=10 counts in at least 6 samples, the smallest group size)
PCA plot on the top 500 most-variable genes post-VST, points colored by condition (AD lesional vs control), with percent variance explained on each axis, and sample_01 labeled
Sample-to-sample Euclidean distance heatmap/matrix on the VST data, samples labeled by condition and by sample ID, with hierarchical clustering

An explicit written verdict on sample_01: whether it clusters with its condition group or departs on PCA/distance measures, whether its low depth alone explains any deviation, and a stated recommendation (keep with size-factor normalization vs exclude) with the reasoning documented -- exclusion is not applied by default per the low-depth-sample handling rule
All outputs (library size table, PCA plot, distance heatmap, verdict text) saved as named files

plan.title: AD lesional vs control skin RNA-seq: sample QC
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question is purely descriptive/QC: before any differential expression testing, characterize the 12-sample cohort (6 AD lesional, 6 control, unpaired, single batch, raw Salmon gene counts, 12000 genes) via library sizes, a variance-stabilized PCA, sample-to-sample distances, and a specific verdict on sample_01, flagged in the data profile as having a library size ~4x below the median. Per the grounded QC procedure (DESeq2 blind-VST + PCA on top-500-variance genes + Euclidean sample-distance heatmap), the low-depth sample is kept through QC, inspected on PCA/distance plots and library-size/detected-gene counts, and only removed with a stated reason -- removal for depth alone is not the default because DESeq2's size-factor normalization already accounts for depth differences. A single step suffices: load counts + metadata, compute raw library sizes and detected-gene counts, run DESeq2 blind VST, PCA (colored by condition), sample-distance heatmap, and produce the depth-outlier verdict as a distinct report artifact.

steps.method: DESeq2 vst(blind) + PCA + sample distance heatmap + library size barplot
